CanvasItem.OnDraw is the protected C# virtual callback for retained drawing, inherited by Entity and Sprite. It records commands during owner-thread canvas preparation and redraw requests are coalesced. Native frame and callback-failure checks cover the initial rectangle/line/texture profile. CanvasLifecycleTests verifies the preceding NotificationDraw/Draw stages and recording failure cleanup. Clipping and further drawing commands remain pending (ADRs 0023/0028).

Reports the active backend after startup selection, on the scene owner thread. Method tokens are gpu/compatibility; driver names come from the active SDL backend. Native Linux Wayland and dummy fallback checks exist. Backend-neutral SDL adaptation follows ADR 0028; other targets and live device recovery remain unimplemented.

Owner-thread readback of the finite root-framebuffer color initialized from the typed project setting. Runtime changes are observed by the initial canvas renderer. Offscreen/multiwindow target clear policies and the full backend matrix remain pending (ADR 0028).

Typed backend-selection setting defaults to gpu and accepts gpu/compatibility. It is sampled at Engine.Run startup; native identities are adapted to SDL GPU and SDL_Renderer under ADR 0028. Feature overrides use the existing registry. Remaining target backends require native verification.

Typed startup fallback policy defaults to true. Under ADR 0028 this reference key projects GPU-to-SDL_Renderer fallback, whose driver need not be OpenGL. False requires GPU initialization; it is not a live recovery switch. Initial dummy/Wayland checks exist, other targets remain unverified.

Typed Color definition defaults to (0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 1) and rejects nonfinite channels. Engine.Run initializes the root framebuffer from the active setting/feature override. The initial renderer is executable; offscreen/multiwindow clear policies remain pending (ADR 0028).

Returns the typed Shader.Mode.CanvasItem value (1) and rejects disposed resources; VerifyResources checks the mode. Particle simulation and drawable-texture shader domains need their own 2D vertical slices (ADR 0028).

ADR 0028 adapts source-code storage/loading to copied compiled SPIR-V artifacts: HLSL/GLSL compile at import/build, including compatible third-party input. Create/Set reject oversized or unaligned payloads before copying, then check the owned snapshot through one structure/reflection/interface path; failed reload preserves the old program and Get returns a copy. This does not expose source text. Runtime checks cover structure and reflected interfaces, not all instruction semantics. Import/cache integration and further shader profiles remain pending.

AtlasTexture implements borrowed nested atlas views under ADRs 0004/0013/0028: floored region sizes and fractional positions, independent zero-axis fallback, margin drawing, crop/opacity queries, FilterClip precedence, ignored tiling, source virtual dispatch and shared full-source material storage. AtlasTextureTests audits defaults, notifications (nested atlas sources only), duplication modes, local-scene ownership, callback failure, disposal and native Linux Wayland compatibility/GPU HLSL/GLSL readback. Typed safety rejects cycles/nonfinite rectangles, checks integer conversions and skips zero-axis drawing; SDL software input truncates fractional UVs, with an explicit boundary-pixel difference asserted in tests under the ADR 0028 fallback precision limit; other platforms retain ADR 0021 verification limits. See docs/classes/AtlasTexture.md.

AnimatedSprite directly inherits Entity under ADR 0008 and implements the pinned animated-sprite source behavior: idle playback, reverse/custom speed, autoplay, frame/progress, nonloop/linear/ping-pong transitions, events, typed packing and virtual texture drawing. AnimatedSpriteTests and AnimatedSpriteRenderingTests cover managed state and native Wayland compatibility/GPU HLSL/GLSL plus dummy readback, actual host timing and callback-failure cleanup. The pinned C++ timing differs from its XML: transitions consume at the previous frame rate and ping-pong retains endpoints; exact boundaries transition on the next positive tick and processing is capped at frame-count plus one iterations. Source behavior is retained rather than silently changed; see docs/classes/AnimatedSprite.md. C# exception/thread/lifetime safety follows existing ADRs; other platforms remain unverified under ADR 0021.

The virtual query supplies the typed extension hook, including ImageTexture logical-to-source coordinate conversion, edge clamping and alpha > 0.1. Missing pixels are treated as opaque. RenderingTextureTests covers size overrides and pixel ownership; additional texture-family behavior remains pending (ADRs 0004/0028).

The reference Texture/Texture2D hierarchy is consolidated as Texture : Resource; ImageTexture derives directly from Texture (ADR 0004). Copied image resources, metadata, duplication and retained drawing execute on the initial backends. Remaining placeholder/family implementations, compressed/integer formats and complete renderer integration prevent a complete type claim (ADRs 0028/0039).

Image inputs are copied; creation and SetImage replace pixel configuration, while Update requires matching dimensions/format/mipmap state and preserves the allocation identity. Validation precedes mutation and Changed is emitted after publication. Managed resource and Linux Wayland GPU/compatibility pixel checks exist. Compressed/integer formats and the full backend matrix remain pending (ADRs 0014/0028/0039).

Nonnegative logical dimensions are stored independently of source pixels; zero preserves the corresponding axis. Size, opacity and texture drawing use the override; SetImage resets it. Update retains source-image dimensions. Existing resource and canvas tests cover this profile; remaining texture/backend behavior requires the rendering integration (ADR 0028).

Inherited ResourceLocalToScene supplies the existing default-false scene-local duplication policy; no redundant ImageTexture property. Resource graph copying exists, but the complete texture serialization/import and scene-instantiation integration remains pending (ADRs 0013/0014/0028).

CanvasItem.OnDraw is the protected C# virtual callback for retained drawing, inherited by Entity and Sprite. It records commands during owner-thread canvas preparation and redraw requests are coalesced. Native frame and callback-failure checks cover the initial rectangle/line/texture profile. CanvasLifecycleTests verifies the preceding NotificationDraw/Draw stages and recording failure cleanup. Clipping and further drawing commands remain pending (ADRs 0023/0028).

Reports the active backend after startup selection, on the scene owner thread. Method tokens are gpu/compatibility; driver names come from the active SDL backend. Native Linux Wayland and dummy fallback checks exist. Backend-neutral SDL adaptation follows ADR 0028; other targets and live device recovery remain unimplemented.

Reports the active backend after startup selection, on the scene owner thread. Method tokens are gpu/compatibility; driver names come from the active SDL backend. Owner-thread readback of the finite root-framebuffer color initialized from the typed project setting. Runtime changes are observed by the initial canvas renderer. Offscreen/multiwindow target clear policies and the full backend matrix remain pending (ADR 0028).

The Engine.Run-owned root renderer exposes finite clear-color changes, retained render-loop enablement and synchronous frame events on the owner thread. Post-draw means submission, not GPU completion/presentation; callback failures propagate after cleanup. Initial native checks exist; multiwindow/offscreen behavior and the remaining renderer surface are not implemented (ADRs 0015/0016/0028).

Typed backend-selection setting defaults to gpu and accepts gpu/compatibility. It is sampled at Engine.Run startup; native identities are adapted to SDL GPU and SDL_Renderer under ADR 0028. Feature overrides use the existing registry. Remaining target backends require native verification.

Typed startup fallback policy defaults to true. Under ADR 0028 this reference key projects GPU-to-SDL_Renderer fallback, whose driver need not be OpenGL. False requires GPU initialization; it is not a live recovery switch. Initial dummy/Wayland checks exist, other targets remain unverified.

Typed Color definition defaults to (0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 1) and rejects nonfinite channels. Engine.Run initializes the root framebuffer from the active setting/feature override. The initial renderer is executable; offscreen/multiwindow clear policies remain pending (ADR 0028).

Returns the typed Shader.Mode.CanvasItem value (1) and rejects disposed resources; VerifyResources checks the mode. Particle simulation and drawable-texture shader domains need their own 2D vertical slices (ADR 0028).

ADR 0028 adapts source-code storage/loading to copied compiled SPIR-V artifacts: HLSL/GLSL compile at import/build, including compatible third-party input. Create/Set reject oversized or unaligned payloads before copying, then check the owned snapshot through one structure/reflection/interface path; failed reload preserves the old program and Get returns a copy. This does not expose source text. Runtime checks cover structure and reflected interfaces, not all instruction semantics. Import/cache integration and further shader profiles remain pending.

Immutable typed PropertyDescriptor lists replace dictionaries for material scalar/vector/fixed-array/texture parameters; built-in TEXTURE is omitted. Reflection validates std140 layouts and bindings; old descriptor snapshots survive reload. Group hints/get_groups, matrices and further uniform types remain pending, so the bool overload is not claimed implemented (ADRs 0005/0028).

Case-sensitive borrowed texture defaults are available at index zero; null clears and material overrides take precedence. Unknown/reserved names, disposed inputs and nonzero indices reject explicitly. Native HLSL/GLSL texture/default/reload checks exist. Sampler arrays and sampler configuration remain pending (ADR 0028).

Typed scalar/vector, copied fixed-array and borrowed Texture getters replace Variant. Names and type/shape are validated; scalar/array defaults are zero and an absent texture override returns null. Reflected Shader defaults resolve at draw time. Matrices, further uniform types, authored value defaults and complete material integration remain pending (ADRs 0001/0005/0028).

Typed ShaderMaterial supports copied scalar/vector/array values, borrowed texture overrides, shared shaders, reload migration and graph duplication; mutations notify Changed in the C# Resource model. HLSL/GLSL native pixel tests cover the documented canvas profile. Further uniform types/defaults, instance uniforms, sampler configuration and full backend behavior remain pending (ADRs 0001/0014/0028).

Executable canvas fragment shaders use the HLSL/GLSL import and shared SPIR-V interface under ADR 0028. Mode.CanvasItem retains value 1. This is a partial 2D profile: other applicable shader domains, import/cache integration and the full backend matrix remain pending.
Spatial surfaces, Sky resources and volumetric fog are 3D domains excluded by the strict 2D product boundary (ADRs 0004/0028).

Trigger: the first drawable-texture/offscreen blit slice must implement its shader entry/interface, target lifecycle and backend checks; ordinary canvas texture sampling does not supply that mode (ADR 0028).

Trigger: the first editor shader-inspection slice must show actual generated backend code and variants through the public engine API; compiling/reflection alone does not implement this editor UI (ADRs 0027/0028).

Sprite maps Sprite2D onto Entity and now inherits through CanvasItem and Node under ADR 0008. Texture/frame/region rendering, typed events, bounds, opacity and PackedScene state are executable in SpriteTests and SpriteRenderingTests on Linux Wayland GPU/compatibility. Inherited sampler repeat/filter now execute through CanvasItem; viewport transform snapping is verified by CanvasPixelSnapTests; editor and accessibility integration remain incomplete; platform evidence follows ADR 0021.

SpriteTests and SpriteRenderingTests verify defaults, local geometry, sheet indexing, regions/flips, retained redraw, resource ownership and notifications, owner-thread guards, callback failures and PackedScene reconstruction. Positive grids must fit Int32.MaxValue; invalid arguments throw before mutation. Grid resizing preserves valid coordinates or silently resets Frame; only explicit Frame/FrameCoords changes emit FrameChanged. Texture reference changes emit TextureChanged; resource content changes only request redraw. Typed events/properties follow ADRs 0004/0005; the accepted inheritance is checked by SceneHierarchyTests under ADR 0008. Native pixel verification covers Wayland GPU/compatibility; wider inherited canvas policies are recorded separately. ItemRectChanged now follows texture_changed and precedes frame_changed/property_list_changed, and covers centering, offset and enabled region changes. No event for transforms, RegionEnabled, flipping, clipping or texture contents; synchronous exception/disposal stages follow typed C# event lifetime rules. SpriteTests verifies these paths against pinned sprite_2d.cpp.

SpriteTests and CanvasPixelSnapTests verify signed dimensions, two-stage integer truncation, centering/offset, empty one-by-one fallback and attached viewport transform snapping (floor(value + 0.5), including negative ties). Detached and vertex-only policies leave inspection bounds fractional. Finite derived geometry is enforced; rendering uses its separate fractional frame size under the pinned contract.

IsPixelOpaque verifies fractional half-open bounds, source alpha, sheet/region selection, custom Texture dispatch and direct-canvas repeat/mirror caches. CanvasSamplingTests covers detached/reattached cache behavior, signed remainder and integer mirror addressing from the pinned native implementation, including fractional mirror query differences from GPU sampling. Viewport sampler defaults do not enter this CPU query. Signed regions retain the accepted drawing flip adaptation. CanvasPixelSnapTests verifies attached viewport transform snapping of the fractional local offset, live query versus retained-command behavior and detached/vertex-only cases. This completes the local source-alpha contract under the existing typed and signed-region adaptations (ADR 0028).

Typed safety rejects cycles/nonfinite rectangles, checks integer conversions and skips zero-axis drawing; SDL software input truncates fractional UVs, with an explicit boundary-pixel difference asserted in tests under the ADR 0028 fallback precision limit; other platforms retain ADR 0021 verification limits. See docs/classes/AtlasTexture.md.
